requirements.requirement: The shared identity dataops exists on both nodes with UID 4500 and GID 4500.
requirements.summary: Both nodes directly report dataops with UID/GID 4500 before and after their respective restarts.

requirements.requirement: node1 exports /srv/nfs/shared, owned by dataops:dataops with mode 2770.
requirements.summary: The active export is restricted to node2, remains active after restart, and the directory repeatedly reports UID/GID 4500:4500 and mode 2770.
Direct findmnt output shows the expected NFS mount at /mnt/shared. The mount, fstab entry, directory metadata, and boot configuration were present after node2 restarted.

requirements.requirement: Files created through either node retain consistent ownership and permissions.
requirements.summary: Files created as dataops on node1 and node2 were observed from the opposite side with UID/GID 4500:4500 and mode 664. Additional post-restart writes retained the same metadata and were visible on node1.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct cross-node behavior checks. The mandatory restart protocol was also completed for both nodes: each had a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity, and recovered service, mount, identity, metadata, data, and write behavior. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently agree with the executor observations. Only minor temporary restart-log residue detracts from hygiene.
limitations: The lifecycle failed-service probes were unsupported because they tested systemd on Alpine; task-specific OpenRC service status checks succeeded, but a provider-wide failed-service inventory was not captured.

Lifecycle package-health output lists changing NFS runtime state files as unowned, so it does not independently validate every installed package file; no actual package inconsistency or damage is demonstrated.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations—package installation, identity creation, NFS configuration, mounting, bounded test writes, and required restarts—had clear roles in implementation or verification. The only unnecessary retained mutations were /tmp/benchmark-reboot.log files created by the restart commands on node1 and node2; lifecycle snapshots show both remained after execution. They are minor, low-risk temporary-file residue. No unrelated troubleshooting mutation, package damage, or conflicting service was demonstrated.
